title: Shirazi Salad
subtitle: Persian cucumber tomato salad
excerpt: Shirazi Salad is a crisp, finely diced Persian salad of tomatoes, onion and fresh herbs dressed with lemon juice and olive oil. It is light, bright and eaten at almost every Persian meal. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Shirazi Salad comes from Shiraz in southern Iran. It is the standard table salad of Iran and appears alongside rice, stews and kebabs at virtually every meal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dice the vegetables and keep them separate. Dress only just before serving or the salad becomes watery.

glossaryTerms.definition: Relating to Shiraz, a city in southern Iran historically important for its poetry, architecture and distinctive style of salad.
The Persian word for fresh herbs and greens, a central element of the Iranian table at every meal.

content.text: salad is about the cut. Everything goes to the same fine dice so no single ingredient dominates a mouthful. The
herbs should be abundant. The dressing is nothing more than lemon juice and olive oil. Serves 4.
Dress this salad right before serving. If it sits dressed for more than 10 minutes the vegetables release water and the salad becomes soggy.
Dice the tomatoes finely to about 5mm pieces. Remove the seeds and any excess juice before dicing or the salad will be wet. Place in a large bowl.
Dice the onion to the same fine size as the tomatoes. If the raw onion flavour is very strong, rinse the diced onion in cold water and drain before adding. Add to the bowl.
Add the chopped mint and parsley to the bowl. Toss gently to combine all the ingredients.
Just before serving, squeeze the lemon juice over the salad and drizzle with olive oil. Toss to coat. Taste and adjust lemon as needed. The salad should be sharp and bright.
Add dried chilli flakes if using. Serve immediately alongside a rice dish, stew or kebabs.

attrs.solution: Remove the seeds from the tomatoes before dicing. Dress the salad only at the moment of serving. The lemon juice draws out vegetable water quickly.
Rinse the diced onion under cold running water for 30 seconds, then drain and pat dry. This removes the harsh sulphur compounds without losing the texture.
Persian salads should have a pronounced lemon acidity. Add more lemon juice a teaspoon at a time. Dried barberries can also be scattered over for extra tartness.

content.text: Shirazi Salad is the universal side dish of Iran. It sits on the table at almost every meal in every part of the country. The fine dice is the defining characteristic and what separates it from rougher chopped salads. In traditional Persian meals it functions as a palate cleanser between bites of rich stew and buttered rice. It also appears as part of mezze spreads.
